title: Admissible pairs and $p$-adic Hodge structures II: the bi-analytic Ax-Lindemann theorem
reviewed_version: arXiv:2308.11064v2, 68-page author manuscript; exact version visible in PDF and arXiv metadata; journal-version equivalence not established
summary: Lemma9.3.3 is false for arbitrary subdiamonds: a two-point neutral GL3 admissible family has empty Hodge-generic locus, while T=S preserves the global motivic Galois group. The main theorem uses the valid pointwise criterion; no central damage established.

problems.title: An arbitrary subdiamond with full family motivic Galois group need not contain a Hodge-generic point

claim.text: T subseteq S intersects the Hodge-generic locus iff MG(G|T,y)=MG(G,y) for some/equivalently any geometric y of T.

assumptions: S arbitrary locally spatial diamond over Spd breveQp, neutral G-admissible pair; no connectedness or irreducibility assumption.
T any subdiamond, including T=S; nonempty in counterexample.
Basicness not required for this auxiliary lemma.

check.input: K=breveQp; W=K e0+K e1+K e2 with semilinear phi(e0)=e0,phi(e1)=p e1,phi(e2)=p e2; N=0. F1^1=<e1+e0,e2>,F2^1=<e1,e2+e0>; F^0=W,F^2=0. S=SpdC coproduct SpdC.
check.all_hypotheses: For every phi-stable D=D0+D1, projection of Fi^1 intersection D to D1 is injective, so tH(D)<=dimD1=tN(D), and tH(W)=tN(W)=2. CFTheoremA yields admissibility; PartI comparison gives exact tensor neutralGL3 family with common W.
check.independent_calculation: Li=W tensor Bdr+ + t^-1Fi^1 tensor Bdr+. Linee2 induced lattices(t^-1B+,B+), linee1(B+,t^-1B+); since both Newton1, each line is admissible only on its designated component.
check.result: The two proper Hodge loci cover S. Generic locus empty, whereas with T=S global group equality tautological.

independent_acceptance.hypothesis_check: The source permits arbitrary locally spatial S and arbitrary subdiamond T, including T=S. The neutral GL3 example has a common isocrystal on the two components and requires no basicness hypothesis for this lemma.
independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: For W with slopes 0,1,1 and F1^1=<e1+e0,e2>, F2^1=<e1,e2+e0>, every stable D decomposes by slope. Projection of D intersect Fi^1 to D1 is injective, proving t_H(D)<=dim D1=t_N(D); total degrees both equal 2. The two filtrations are therefore weakly admissible. Each of the slope-one lines e1 and e2 is admissible on exactly one component. Their two proper Hodge loci cover the disjoint two-point base S. Hodge-generic locus is empty, although T=S makes equality of the family motivic Galois groups tautological.

external_interface_check.observation: Actually displayed and read author PDF page 2: complete discretely valued characteristic-zero field with perfect residue field and Theorem A weak admissibility implies admissibility. Checked the needed theorem interface, not its proof.

independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: The proof tests containment in one proper Hodge locus; this does not imply intersection of T with the complement of the union. Restricting T to a geometric point gives the valid criterion used by Theorem 9.1.3. For general nonempty T, replacing the assertion by noncontainment in every single proper Hodge locus gives the family-group criterion. The subsequent density lemma has additional geometric hypotheses and expressly does not depend on this lemma.
independent_acceptance.impact: Local unused generality is false; no failure of the stated core pointwise use or generic-density theorem is established. Minor retained on actual dependency impact.

independent_acceptance.summary: Independent focused acceptance confirms the single local quantifier defect in Lemma 9.3.3 of arXiv:2308.11064v2 dated 28 February 2025. The pointwise use in the core argument remains valid; retain Minor. No scientific report text change is required.
independent_acceptance.scope: Check of the existing arbitrary-subdiamond allegation, its admissibility construction, pointwise repair, original lemma and surrounding generic-density argument; no equivalence to the unavailable journal version and no full reproof of external foundations.
independent_acceptance.conclusion: Retain M25-0132-P1 as Minor. The common family group need not be attained at a point of an arbitrary disconnected subdiamond; no counterexample to the main Ax-Lindemann theorem is established.
